title: Luxury and Investigation in Daniel Vorcaro's Mansions
seoTitle: Luxury and investigation in Daniel Vorcaro's mansions
subtitle: Federal Police search reveals details of architecture, security, and seized assets
excerpt: Federal Police found high-end amenities, safes, an underground wine cellar, and artworks in Daniel Vorcaro's three residences during a probe into billion-dollar fraud.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On the morning of November 18, 2025, the Federal Police raided three high-end properties linked to Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, while he remained in custody after being intercepted at Guarulhos Airport. The searches, conducted in São Paulo, Brasília, and Belo Horizonte, explain the sudden public interest in the banker's mansions.

Daniel Vorcaro's Mansions in São Paulo

Located in the Jardim América neighborhood, the São Paulo house was described as the most heavily guarded and the one the owner used most frequently. The property features spas, bars, gyms, cinema rooms, swimming pools, three safes – one of which had to be forced open due to a missing combination – and a spacious underground wine cellar containing hundreds of high-value wines. Among the seized belongings were Rolex, Audemars Piguet, and Richard Mille watches, as well as a 6-terabyte hard drive and a diamond necklace marked with the letter D.

The Interior of the Brasília Residence

Located in Lago Sul, the property primarily served for receptions and meetings, according to Federal Police documentation. The house offers views of Lake Paranoá and the JK Bridge, meeting rooms, and few personal items. Office files contained papers with lists of expensive wines and a memorandum about farms, as well as folders bearing the emblems of the Chamber of Deputies and Banco de Brasília (BRB).

The Belo Horizonte Property

In the Belvedere neighborhood, the mansion combines three contiguous plots of land that transform into spacious leisure areas: gourmet areas with bars, gyms, a spa, sports courts, and relaxation spaces. Unlike the other residences, agents found empty closets and no valuable assets, according to the housekeeper who reported that the location was only used as a leisure retreat.

Assets Seized During the Searches

In addition to the luxury items in the houses, the operation resulted in the seizure of R$290,000 in Brazilian notes and dollars stored in a drawer safe, a painting attributed to the French artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir, a painting with the phrase “we kill for peace,” and armored vehicles. The most significant find, however, was Vorcaro's cell phone, seized at the airport, whose contents allowed for the extraction of conversations with members of the Judiciary, Legislative, and Executive branches, expanding the scope of the investigation into Banco Master's billion-dollar frauds.

With information from O GLOBO, Revista Oeste, InfoMoney.
